(correct, DB confirms active). Turn 2 'How many companies do we have in total?' -> 'QA-SWARM-TEST-CO-VIA-CHAT: restored.' (repeats turn 1's answer). Turn 3 'yes' -> '20 companies in total.' controls.D — hard reload, ORG B selected: "You're working in SEM Technologies LLC. It has 9 projects." Unchanged.

bugs.root_cause_isolation: CONTROL C IS DECISIVE AND RULES OUT THE HYPOTHESIS THIS TEST WAS DESIGNED TO CONFIRM. A FRESH channel with ORG B selected returns the same answer as a FRESH channel with ORG A selected. The reply is INVARIANT under the selector, so there is no Org-A state for history to carry over and the defect cannot be StaleChannelContextOverridesCurrentOrgScope. The selector is simply never transmitted to the chat request; Brain then INFERS a default ("the ultimate holding entity") from workspace data. Control D rules out stale client state (hard reload, unchanged).
bugs.secondary_finding_history_rationalizatio: Control B is still notable on its own terms: Brain said "Based on the prior conversation history, you are working in SEM Technologies LLC" — it CITED history as the source for org identity. Because fresh channels produce the same answer, history is NOT the cause; it is a post-hoc rationalisation of an answer Brain would have given anyway. Recorded so a reader does not mistake the citation for the mechanism.
bugs.partial_precedence_win: Control B ALSO shows OTM §2 precedence working where it is wired: Brain distrusted the stale narrative count, re-read context.projects, and corrected "9 projects in SEM Technologies LLC" to "0 projects directly assigned to it". Fresh canonical data beat conversational history for the COUNT even though it could not for the org IDENTITY — because identity had no canonical source to read.
bugs.count_defect_still_present: In controls A, C and D the workspace-wide total (9 projects across all companies) is asserted as "9 projects exist in it" for a named org that Brain's own fresh read says owns 0. Same family as BUG-024 (count-by-inference, CLAUDE.md §26).
bugs.security_classification: NOT AN AUTH BYPASS. The account under test is the FOUNDER, who is legitimately entitled to every company in the workspace, so no permission boundary was crossed and no data was disclosed that this caller may not see. This is category (A) in the founder's own framing: workspace-wide data incorrectly described as selected-org data — a serious truth/tenant-context defect, not a cross-tenant leak. The test that could turn this into a disclosure finding is a NON-FOUNDER persona in a browser, which remains BLOCKED for want of a second credential.
bugs.why_p1: P1 on truth, not on authorization. A multi-org operator asks Brain a question with an organization selected and receives an answer about a DIFFERENT organization, labelled as theirs, with a workspace-wide number presented as that organization's. Every Brain answer about "my organization" is currently untrustworthy in a multi-org workspace, and the failure is silent - the reply never says its scope is workspace-wide.
bugs.relationship_to_bug_015: BUG-015 is the UI-surface scoping matrix and is NOT broadened by this. This is the chat/grounding half, filed separately because the mechanism is different: the UI surfaces DO receive the selection and five of them ignore it, whereas chat never receives it at all.
bugs.regression_requirement: With org X selected, a FRESH chat channel asked "which organization am I working in?" must name X (or state explicitly that its answer is workspace-wide). Assert the reply differs when the selector differs — the A/C invariance above is the exact regression signature. Additionally assert any count attributed to a named org equals an aggregate for THAT org, not the workspace.
bugs.home_pc_pointer: The chat request body carries command / channelId / imageBase64; no organization field is present, and getActiveProvider/buildContext have no org parameter. Work PC did not modify the source; this is a pointer, not a diagnosis.
bugs._qa_boundary: Browser + product paths only. One project created via the product UI as a registered fixture.
bugs.per_verifier_instruction: Closure requires an independent Work-PC rerun of controls A and C; identical answers under different selectors is the failure. The implementation PC may not self-certify.

bugs.title: Brain Chat asserts that an EXISTING company "does not exist in the database" - context truncation is reported as canonical non-existence, and the honest scope-limited phrasing it produced one turn earlier is ABANDONED for a false absolute
bugs.ai_truth_classification: FABRICATED_ABSENCE (proposed new class - the polarity mirror of FALSE_SUCCESS). Adjacent to but NOT the same as GROUNDING_GAP: the gap is the cause, the defect is asserting the gap as canonical fact.
bugs.build_under_test: EDGE v94 (v92 source) / WEB SHA UNKNOWN
bugs.discovered_while: Running the BUG-010 root-cause expansion (CLAUDE.md section 13) - re-testing the person-assignment variant while deliberately forcing the clarification branch. Not the defect the test was looking for.
bugs.ground_truth: EXISTS AND IS ACTIVE. /companies at All Organizations, 03:46:11Z: row 13 of 14 - "QA-C002-RENAMED-X | Business unit | - | active | 5 people | 0". It is also the parent company of the department created minutes earlier in this same session, and it appears in the /departments company picker and in the org switcher.
reproduction: Turn 1: "Assign QA-C002-PENDING-01 to the company QA-C002-RENAMED-X."

Turn 1 reply (HONEST, correctly scope-limited): "I need to clarify what you mean by 'assign.' QA-C002-PENDING-01 is a person (currently with no company assigned). QA-C002-RENAMED-X is not in my current view - I don't see a company by that name. Did you mean to assign this person to an existing company, or did you mean something else?"
Turn 2: "Yes, assign that person to QA-C002-RENAMED-X."

Turn 2 reply (FALSE ABSOLUTE): "I don't see a company named QA-C002-RENAMED-X in the database. The company you're referring to doesn't exist under that name. Could you clarify which company you meant, or confirm the correct company name?"
bugs.expected: A truthful statement of scope: "not in my current view" / "outside the context I can see" - or a canonical existence check. What must never happen is an unqualified claim about what is or is not IN THE DATABASE when the answer is derived from a truncated context window.
bugs.actual: Turn 2 asserts non-existence twice, and both assertions are canonical in form: "in the database" and "doesn't exist under that name". The company exists and is active.
bugs.the_escalation_is_the_finding: The SAME session, ONE TURN APART, produced both framings for the SAME entity: turn 1 said "is not in my current view" (true, scope-limited, exactly right) and turn 2 said "doesn't exist in the database" (false, canonical). The system demonstrably HAS the correct framing available and abandoned it when pressed. This is not a missing capability; it is a truthfulness regression across turns under user insistence - which is the worst possible direction, because user insistence is precisely when a founder is relying on the answer.
bugs.independent_corroboration_same_entity: During BUG-028 controls the SAME company was described correctly as "belongs to a company not visible in this context (company_id 8fdad6e2-...)". Same entity, same absence from context, honest framing. That rules out "the model cannot tell the difference" - it can, and does, elsewhere.
bugs.root_cause_hypothesis: The company almost certainly falls outside the capped context list (it is row 13 of 14, and Brain volunteered its own truncation bound earlier the same session: "I cannot rule out that a different project with the new name exists outside the capped project list"). Truncation is the CAUSE. The DEFECT is that truncation is surfaced to the user as canonical non-existence rather than as limited scope. Work PC did not read the sem-ai-command source; this is a pointer, not a diagnosis.
bugs.governing_rule_violated: CLAUDE.md section 6 (AI context completeness) is explicit and this is a direct violation: "Never present truncated data as complete data." The section requires the model to know returnedCount / totalCount / isTruncated / retrievalScope and to say "30 of 69 active tasks shown", not "there are 30 tasks". The same requirement applies to existence: absence from a truncated window is not absence from the database.
bugs.blast_radius: NO DATA WAS CHANGED - the operation was refused, which is the correct outcome for the assign request itself. The damage is decision-integrity, and it is worse than it first looks in two directions. (1) DUPLICATE CREATION: a founder told a company does not exist may create it again, which is a real write driven by a false read. (2) FALSE DATA-LOSS INCIDENT: a founder told an entity they created is absent from the database may reasonably conclude data was lost and escalate. Both are founder actions caused by a confident false statement.
bugs.why_p1: P1 on truth, consistent with how BUG-002 and BUG-010 are rated. It is a confident, unqualified, canonical-sounding false statement about database contents, produced under user insistence, on an entity the user just named. It is also the polarity mirror of the existing FALSE_SUCCESS class - the product can both claim a mutation that did not happen and deny an entity that does exist. Any product built on "ask Brain about your data" is unreliable in BOTH directions.
bugs.not_p0: No authorization boundary was crossed and no data was mutated or disclosed. The founder is entitled to see this company.

relationship_to_other_bugs.BUG-002 / FALSE_SUCCESS: MIRROR IMAGE, same family, opposite polarity. BUG-002 claims a mutation that did not occur; BUG-029 denies an entity that does exist. Filed separately because the mechanism differs - BUG-002 is capability-absence not surfaced as refusal, BUG-029 is context-truncation not surfaced as scope.
relationship_to_other_bugs.BUG-017 (context window): BUG-017 is the truncation itself. BUG-029 is the MISREPORTING of truncation. Deliberately not merged: fixing the window size would not fix the false phrasing, and fixing the phrasing would not need the window fixed. They are independently closable.
relationship_to_other_bugs.BUG-024 / count-by-inference: Same governing rule (CLAUDE.md section 6). BUG-024 is truncated data presented as complete COUNTS; BUG-029 is truncated data presented as complete EXISTENCE. Worth a joint fix if one is designed - both need isTruncated/retrievalScope surfaced to the model and reflected in its language.
relationship_to_other_bugs.BUG-010: Found while expanding BUG-010, but NOT a BUG-010 instance and not merged. No fabricated claim was persisted; the false statement is generated fresh from a truncated read.

bugs.regression_requirement: REQUIRED, permanent. For an entity that EXISTS but falls outside the context window, any Brain statement about its existence must be scope-qualified. Assert that the reply does NOT contain an unqualified non-existence claim ("does not exist", "no such", "not in the database") for an entity that a canonical query proves present. The test must include the MULTI-TURN form: ask once, then RE-ASSERT the entity name, because the observed failure only escalated to the false absolute on the second turn. A single-turn test would have PASSED here.
bugs.implementation_recommendation: Do not fix by prompt wording alone. The model already produces the correct phrasing sometimes, so the wording is not the missing piece - what is missing is a hard distinction the model cannot collapse. Structural options for Home PC: (1) surface isTruncated / totalCount / retrievalScope into the context pack so the model can SEE that its view is partial (CLAUDE.md section 6 already requires this and it would serve BUG-024 at the same time); (2) route existence questions to a canonical count/exists query rather than to the truncated list, per CLAUDE.md section 26 - existence is a deterministic fact and section 26 forbids deriving deterministic facts from a truncated context array.
bugs._qa_boundary: Browser + product paths only. Zero mutations. The assign operation was refused by the product, which is correct; QA did not force it through by any other path.
bugs.per_verifier_instruction: Closure requires an independent Work-PC reproduction of the TWO-TURN sequence against a then-deployed build with a stated WEB_SHA. The implementation PC may not self-certify. A single-turn probe is not sufficient evidence of a fix.
